question_types.description: Compute summary statistics using Excel functions.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Compute the mean yield (bu/ac) across all 120 fields.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Compute the median yield.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Compute the sample standard deviation of yield.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Compute the 90th percentile of yield. Explain what it means in one sentence.
parts.answer: 52.50 bu/ac — 90% of fields yielded this or less.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Is the mean or the median higher? What does this tell you about the shape of the distribution?
parts.answer: The median (46.25) is higher than the mean (45.65), indicating a slight left skew — some low-yielding fields pull the mean down.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Compute the mean and median of the acres column.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Compute Q1 and Q3 of yield.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Compute the IQR of yield.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Compute the sample variance of yield. What are its units?
parts.answer: 33.66 (bu/ac)². Units are squared because variance squares the deviations.

parts.label: e
parts.text: What is the range of yield? (max minus min)

question_types.description: Use COUNTIF, SUMIF, AVERAGEIF, XLOOKUP, and IF to answer questions about subsets of the data.

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many fields have a yield strictly greater than 50 bu/ac?

parts.label: b
parts.text: What is the average yield in the South region? Central? North?

parts.label: c
parts.text: Compute total production (bushels) across all fields. (Production = yield × acres.)

parts.label: d
parts.text: Use a lookup function to find the variety planted in field F050.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Write a formula that classifies each field as "Low" (yield < 40), "Medium" (40–50), or "High" (above 50). Apply it to all rows.
parts.answer: Low / Medium / High labels in a new column

parts.label: a
parts.text: What is the total production (bushels) in the South region only?

parts.label: b
parts.text: How many fields are both irrigated AND in the Central region?
parts.answer: Use COUNTIFS — count varies by dataset

parts.label: c
parts.text: What is the average yield of irrigated fields? Of non-irrigated fields?

parts.label: d
parts.text: Use a lookup to find the variety and acres for field F100.

parts.label: e
parts.text: How many fields in the North region have a yield above the overall mean?
parts.answer: Use COUNTIFS with the computed mean

question_types.description: Build a PivotTable to summarize data by categories.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Create a PivotTable showing the average yield by region. Which region has the highest average?

parts.label: b
parts.text: Expand the PivotTable to show average yield by region AND variety (regions on rows, varieties on columns). Which region-variety combination has the highest average?

parts.label: c
parts.text: Create a second PivotTable showing total acres by variety. Which variety has the most total acreage?

parts.label: d
parts.text: How many fields are in each region? (Use the Count function in your PivotTable.)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Create a PivotTable showing average yield by variety. Which variety performs best on average?

parts.label: b
parts.text: Add a filter to your PivotTable to show only irrigated fields. Does the ranking of varieties change?
parts.answer: Add irrigated to Filters, select TRUE. Compare rankings.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Create a PivotTable showing total production (yield × acres) by region. Which region produces the most canola in total?
parts.answer: Requires a helper column yield*acres, then PivotTable on that column by region.
parts.formula: Helper column =D2*E2, then PivotTable: region → Rows, helper → Values (Sum)

parts.label: d
parts.text: Show the count of fields by region and irrigated status (regions on rows, irrigated on columns).
parts.answer: PivotTable: region → Rows, irrigated → Columns, field_id → Values (Count)

question_types.description: Create and interpret histograms and box-and-whisker plots.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Create a histogram of yield_bu_ac for all 120 fields. Use approximately 10–15 bins. Give your chart a descriptive title and label both axes.
parts.answer: Histogram with bell-shaped, slightly left-skewed distribution centred around 45–47 bu/ac.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Based on your histogram, is the distribution symmetric, left-skewed, or right-skewed?
parts.answer: Slightly left-skewed (longer tail on the low end).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Are there any apparent outliers? If so, approximately what yield values?
parts.answer: Possible outliers near 29 bu/ac at the low end.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Create a box-and-whisker plot comparing yield_bu_ac across the three regions (South, Central, North). Give your chart a descriptive title and label both axes.
parts.answer: Three boxes showing Central highest, South lowest and most variable.
parts.formula: Insert → Statistical Chart → Box and Whisker

parts.label: b
parts.text: Which region has the highest median yield?

parts.label: c
parts.text: Which region has the most variability in yield (widest box)? What does this suggest about farming conditions in that region?
parts.answer: South has the widest box (IQR ≈ 9.6). This suggests more variable growing conditions — possibly more weather risk or more heterogeneous soil quality.
